utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. We continue with the evidence of Mr. Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Dobar dan, Gospodin Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your examination by Mr. Lukic will continue in the moment. Please bear in mind that the solemn declaration to speak the truth which you gave at the outset of your evidence continues to apply until that evidence is completed. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning from me, too, Mr. Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have Exhibit 6D269 brought up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see the document now. Who and when adopted this document -- probably issued is the better word.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chief of the public security, Colonel-General Vlastimir Djordjevic on the 18th of February, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please go to the last page to see if he signed it as well.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was this sent to? Who is it addressed to?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To all the units of the public security at the ministry's HQ in Belgrade; to all the secretariats, 33 of them; to the ministry staff in Pristina; to the border police stations, a total of 35 of those, as we see; and to the state security department, to the chief, to the attention of the chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need the entire document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell us what it's about.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was adopted just before the start of the NATO aggression, before the air-strikes began, and this is the Ministry of the Interior preparing for that sort of situation. It's clear if you look at the measures being ordered here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please go to the last page with item 16. Item 16, what specifically is being ordered there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First and foremost, full cooperation with the VJ units, exchange of information, and to have joint action and cooperation between this ministry and the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have 6D238.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who adopted this document and when?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was adopted by Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic on the 24th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who is it addressed to?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To everyone, same as the previous document, but it wasn't addressed to the public security sector -- state security sector.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please go to paragraph 1 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please read this.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Since on the 23rd of March, 1999, the federal government declared a state of imminent threat of war, it is necessary to step up the measures ordered in our dispatch number 312 dated the 18th of February, 1999, with particular emphasis on the following ..." My apologies. Should I repeat anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, but I do have to ask you one thing. Is this dispatch in reference to the previous one that we looked at?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please go to item 7 on the next page, it's the last paragraph in the English, it's page 2. Item number 7. Can you read this, please.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Establish full cooperation with units of the VJ. There should be exchange of information on movements, preparations, and axes of movement of the aggressor forces. Organize, if necessary, concerted action by the ministry and the VJ to keep the aggressor forces from forcing their entry into FRY territory."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is this paragraph in relation to?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same as the paragraph that we were looking at in that previous document. This is about cooperation, about concerted action, and about exchange of information between the police on the one hand and the army on the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have 6D132.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, who adopted this document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who is it addressed to?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same addressees as the previous document, all the secretariats, the staff, organizational units back in the ministry, and units of the border police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you look at paragraph 1, please, and can you read it for us?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The federal government after the air-strikes carried out by NATO against our country has declared a state of war. In order to have full mobility and preparedness for carrying out all jobs and assignments that the ministry is in charge of in wartime, in keeping with defence plans and the specific security situation prevailing in the area, secretariat," and I think this is probably a typo, "it is necessary to step up measures ordered in our dispatches dated the 18th of February and the 24th of March, 1999."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So is this a reference to the previous two dispatches that we looked at?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we please go to item 2 now, and read it for us, if you can.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a rather poor copy but I'll do my best. "Carry out the mobilisation of the needed amount of reserve police officers in order to step up general police activity, patrol activity, operative and other forms of activity, with the objective of maintaining law and public law -- law and order stable. Preventing any crimes from being committed or criminal offences, security." It probably reads: "Securing or guarding some persons," because this is a very poor copy and I can't really see what it says, therefore I'm just guessing, "installations and carrying out other jobs and duties."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the minister of the interior of the Republic of Serbia giving an order, so what is this order, "nalog," about?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's for the needed amount of police reserves to be involved to step up the activities of all the police's organizational units and to prevent crimes or criminal offences, as well as to secure certain facilities or buildings. Needless to say, the secretariats themselves know that they have to prevent any crimes or criminal offences from being committed and that they have to track down their perpetrators, but given this newly arisen situation, something like this might have been taken advantage of by certain individuals and groups, the situation I mean would have been taken advantage of by individuals and groups to carry out certain crimes, and that's probably why the ministry is focusing on this issue here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm perfectly aware of the fact that this is a very poor copy, but can we please try to read the last paragraph of this document.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Coordinate with VJ units in order to prevent the aggressor's forced entry into FRY territory."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Again, what is the minister ordering here?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To have the necessary degree of coordination with the VJ in defending the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were these dispatches acted upon?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, although, as they say, we had all expected that the war would never come, that a peaceful solution would after all be found. I know this was the position taken by the state leadership, by the army, by the police. They were all expecting this and they all wanted this to happen, the entire nation did, needless to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have 6D609. No translation for this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You will have to tell us who is sending it, when it was made, and who the addressee appears to be?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I would like to raise my standard objection about this and proceed as we have in the past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How many of these untranslated documents are going to be presented, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm not hearing you very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that this is the one untranslated. We had one yesterday and this should be the untranslated document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, please read, don't comment. The header of this document, the addressees, the first paragraph, up to this word here, "Glogovac, OUP Glogovac." Just slowly, please, for the interpreters to be able to follow.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The header reads: "MUP of the Republic of Serbia, public security sector, dispatch number 548, the 17th of March, 1999." The document was addressed to the SUP offices in Kragujevac, Jagodina, Smederevo, Pozarevac, Zajecar Bor, Belgrade, Pristina, and Kosovska Mitrovica, the chief, to the chief. The commands of the 37th and 86th PJP Detachments in Kragujevac to the commander, the MUP staff in Pristina to the head, and to the administration for joint activities in the ministry's HQ to the chief. The first paragraph reads: "The involvement of members of the 36th and 86th Detachments of the PJP, who on the 23rd of February, 1999, were dispatched to help out the secretariats of the interior in Pristina, in Kosovska Mitrovica shall terminate on the 24th of March, 1999. In order to have them replaced, it is necessary to carry out preparations, and on this day under the establishment, dispatch to OUP Glogovac from the Kragujevac SUP, the 1st Company of the 36th PJP Detachment. On the Jagodina SUP, the 2nd Company of the 36th PJP Detachment." Do you want me to read on?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, thank you. No need for that. That will do because my question is: Does this document show that on the 17th of March the MUP of the Republic of Serbia had its headquarters planned a replacement of PJP units, not the sending of new units. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct and that can be seen from the text of the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When was this replacement supposed to take place?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The replacement was supposed to take place on the 24th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just want to inform Your Honours that it seems that we have one more un -- that we have one more untranslated document, it would be used at the very end of this examination, but it's 6D237.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, I'll raise my objection at that time, but with this one while we still have it up, normally this might be something I would address on my cross-exam, but because it's not translated, could I request that the witness be asked to read what's stamped on the bottom of both pages and any signature, what he can tell us about who this is from, sort of for authenticity purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you deal with that, please, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, at the bottom of both pages --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I haven't found the document. What was the number you said?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 6D609, and you have it on the screen too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, it's the one that you're dealing with at the moment, forget the other one that Mr. Lukic referred to, back to the one you've just read and you'll see now that the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So we see at the bottom of each and every page we see a text in Cyrillic, and could you read for us what this says, this is a text that is obviously not part of the document.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Copy faithful to the original, authorised official, sergeant first -- staff sergeant or sergeant first class Ljiljana Veselinovic, the 21st of June, 2006, signed by Ljiljana Veselinovic. It's also on the second page rather the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know what this is all about?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can assume that this copy was made precisely by Mrs. Ljiljana Veselinovic from the original and she signed that because that is what her text says, that this is a copy that is an authentic copy faithful to the original and she confirms that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this enough, Your Honour? Is this enough or I should examine further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you content with that, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, what was the behaviour of the KLA after the 20th of March, 1999, when the KVM left Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That can be seen from certain documents that the so-called KLA after the verification mission left Kosovo and Metohija intensified its terrorist activity by carrying out attacks against citizens, both in urban areas and outside urban areas. Civilians were killed, policemen were killed. So once the KVM left the intensity of activity was stepped up.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 6D614 on e-court page 690 in both versions, B/C/S and English. I am sorry. We don't have a translation, so we're -- I'm not going to use it. It's been translated only up to page 590, but I will give some examples from this document in terms of attacks against policemen. It is item 539, 540, 541, 542, 543, 544, 545, 546, all these items being on page 690, and then on page 691, in both versions, 547, and I made an omission. On page 690 there is also 549 and 550. In relation to attacks against civilians, on page 690, there is 551, 552, and 553. Now I would like to ask for the following document to be called up on e-court, 6D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, what is this document, 6D614?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's a big document that encompasses criminal reports from Kosovo that were collected after the war, so it does not represent all the criminal cases, but the cases that were found after the withdrawal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: For the avoidance of any doubt, what you've just done by reading these items does not amount to admission of any of this document. I gathered from what you said before that you intend to submit this in some other way for our consideration. So we will ignore the reference to these various paragraphs at this stage and wait until we see whether the document is admitted in some way. If it is, then we will obviously come back and note that in the context of this evidence you referred to these particular paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, now we should have a look at 6D291. Who sent this document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was sent by the chief of the public security sector, General Vlastimir Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When was it sent?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sent on the 21st of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was it sent to?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sent to a number of secretariats. If necessary, I'm going to read them all out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Secretariats from Kosovo, secretariats from the interior of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was sent to a number of secretariats in the central part of Serbia and secretariats in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who else?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the commands of the 21st, 22nd, 23rd, 35th, 36th, and 37th PJP Detachments in Novi Sad, Belgrade, Uzice, Kragujevac, and Nis, the commander, and to the head of the MUP staff in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are the headquarters of all of these PJP detachments outside Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What can now be seen from the first paragraph, please?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to read it or do you want me to read it and then give you my comments?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can give us your comments straight away, if you've read it.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This paragraph shows that in order to carry out special security tasks on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, the mentioned detachments are being sent, namely on the 22nd of March, that they are being sent to carry out their regular work to provide assistance to the following secretariats in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were these PJP detachments sent to Kosovo to be at the disposal of the MUP staff in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you can see from here that they're being sent to the secretariats in Kosovo to assist them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After the KVM left, who came to Kosovo and Metohija from the MUP leaders?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generals Lazarevic and -- Generals Djordjevic and Stevanovic -- no, sorry, I think it was only Stevanovic who came.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have a mistake here, I think, in the transcript, the name of General Lazarevic appears. Did you mention him?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I mentioned Djordjevic and Stevanovic, but I made a mistake, it was General Stevanovic who came.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were meetings held with the SUP chiefs and detachment commanders, commanders of the PJP detachments, that is?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was principally discussed?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was principally discussed were the coming tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please call up in e-court 6D238.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. I interrupted you, but on page 1, paragraph 2 of this document what is primarily insisted upon there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is primarily insisted upon there is, among other things, stepped-up activity in carrying out operative and other activities, and also taking measures energetically to prevent crimes and misdemeanours, particularly those involving violence, which could have been expected in that kind of a situation. Of course the focus was on preventing any danger to human lives and their property, so that meant the protection of the population in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was that discussed at the meetings you had with commanders of the detachments and the -- of the PJPs and with the chiefs of SUPs?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was done regularly when these meetings were held, and the emphasis was always on lawful conduct and taking all measures to observe regulations governing police work to a maximum as well as protect the civilian population. That was also done by way of certain documents, and there was quite a bit of that. That's to say it wasn't done only at meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to move on to the time of war and bombing, that is to say after the 24th of March, 1999. Are you aware of the case of a killing committed in Podujevo at the very beginning of the war carried out by the reserve members of the SAJ?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am aware of that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could anyone from the staff decide that any police unit should have a reserve force and how that force would be engaged?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please let's clarify this. It is one thing to have a reserve force and it is another thing to engage it. All police units according to the law had their reserve force, or rather, the wartime assignments of these units involved a reserve force and their involvement could only be ordered by the minister of the interior or perhaps a person that he would authorise to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see this from this document, 6D132, paragraph 2, who has the power to mobilise the reserve force of the police?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you say 132?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, 6D132.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see this from paragraph 2, where the minister himself orders the mobilisation of the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who at that time had the exclusive authority to actually employ or engage the reserve force of the police?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the orders of the minister, this was done by the units that actually had the reserve force, so the secretariats, primarily the secretariats, and there were reserve forces in the headquarters of the ministry, some units did have their reserve force in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can the minister delegate this authority to anyone else?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this time he did it himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did it ever happen that the minister -- as regards this authority to engage the reserve force and to mobilise the reserve forces of the Ministry of the Interior in Kosovo and Metohija, to delegate it to anyone in the staff?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this was not done ever. It was usually delegated to the chief of the public security sector or to some associate of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did you learn that some of the reservists from the SAJ were again engaged in Kosovo and Metohija, the ones who had been there before?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned that while I was being proofed for my testimony here at this trial, because I know that after this event that this unit was removed from there, that they were prosecuted, but the first time that I heard that they had gone back to Kosovo was when I was being proofed for my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when was the first time that you heard about the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about the Skorpions when they were put on trial; I saw it on TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I would like us to look --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I be clear, what are we talking about when we talk about the Skorpions? What event are we talking about and in what --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh, it's the same?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Throughout this you have been describing them as the reserve force of the SAJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And that's the same as what we've already heard described as the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] So could we please have P1996 up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just finally, Mr. Mijatovic, when were the Skorpions put on trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I couldn't tell you. I know that it was after the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Roughly how long after the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really couldn't tell you. I watch TV seldom -- in fact, I sometimes watch the daily news and that's where I saw that. I saw an item on the evening news, that they were being put on trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When did you retire from the service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 31st of December, 2004.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Was it after that, this trial?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really couldn't be any more specific than this, but I'm sure that it was after the war and after the police and the army pulled out of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that would be 1999, but are you saying it might even have been after 2004?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really couldn't tell you when it was because I don't recall, but I do recall seeing that on the news that the Skorpions were being put on -- were on trial, but I wasn't quite sure what the crimes were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it also might be that there were two proceedings, one instigated immediately after the war and another one when the term "Skorpions" was used for the first time might be -- yeah, during the Milosevic trial, that was the first time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's quite -- that's completely different, though, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, yeah, but the same unit was in Bosnia --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but it's not events in 1999 that featured in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, no, no, but the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, let's just proceed with the evidence. The witness obviously knows nothing about this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, you have this document, P1996, in front of you. Could you please go to page 8 in English, that would be page 10, the first paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And just below the first set of bullet points, "in the further course ..."

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In the further course ..."?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that where you should start, and then you should read -- I do apologise, I'm a little bit mixed up. Could you please turn to page 1 and tell us what this document is, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the minutes from a meeting held at the staff in Pristina involving the police leadership in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did you hear about the fact that Dragan Ilic was, in fact, in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And on page 8 of this document, the section that I referred you to before, is it clear from this that he actually participated in the debate at this meeting in the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was he doing in the seat or headquarters of the MUP in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Dragan Ilic was the chief of the crime police in the MUP headquarters in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know what his role was in May?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go to the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what was the role of Dragan Ilic in March 1999 in Kosovo and Metohija, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can see from the minutes, Dragan Ilic had come, since he was in charge of the organizational units fighting crime, he had come to make them step up their work, to improve the organization, and, as we can see from here, he had a meeting with the chiefs of the criminal police departments in the secretariats in Kosovo and Metohija. A plan was drafted to sanitize the territory, and it was distributed to the chiefs, and he informed the people present at the meeting accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And why did Dragan Ilic present this briefing at the MUP staff meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to inform the other leaders about that because only the chiefs of the criminal police departments in the secretariats were present when he distributed the plan, and this was a meeting of a different kind. It was attended by the chiefs of the secretariats, part of the staff, Generals Stevanovic, Lukic, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the date of this meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 7th of May, 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've -- you were asked a question: What was his role in May? And then you were asked: What was his role in March? I take it all of this relates to May then, Mr. Lukic, does it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It doesn't, sorry. There was no answer to the question: Do you know what his role was in May? And then you asked: What was the role in March? Now, the answer's given from the minutes and the minutes seem to relate to a meeting in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right, my mistake, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but the witness now seems to say, no, the answer relates to March, so I'm totally confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll try to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, the activities of Mr. Ilic are -- do they pertain to May or March 1999?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's May. I didn't mention March I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I did. It was my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was talking about May.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We indicated that we would be using Exhibit 4D3, but it's available only in Serbian, whereas Exhibit P985 is available both in English and in Serbian. So if my learned friend Mr. Hannis is not opposed to it, I would like to use the Prosecution exhibit so that we can avail ourselves of the translation. It is the Law on Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, could you please go to page 2 of this exhibit and tell us what you know about the manner in which anti-terrorist actions were planned and carried out in 1999. Let's just clear one thing up. Yesterday I asked you about the planning in the course of 1998, and when I went through my questions I don't think that they were specific enough. When we talked about the planning of anti-terrorist actions in 1998 and when we talked about, or rather, when you spoke about the excerpts of the maps that you received from the Army of Yugoslavia, did this pertain to joint actions carried out by both the MUP -- the police forces and the Army of Yugoslavia; or both to joint actions and actions carried out separately by the police?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It pertained only to joint actions that the police carried out, not the actions that the secretariats or organizational units of the MUP carried out themselves. It pertained only to joint actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now that we are on this topic, were there any actions that were carried out only by the police?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what actions are you referring to, but the police definitely carried out its regular activities and among them were actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Independent anti-terrorist actions, that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was some small-scale actions that were planned by the secretariats in order to capture the perpetrators of crimes and to arrest the terrorists, but there were no large-scale actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, those plans that were drafted by the secretariats, were they similar to the military plans? Were there maps drawn, orders, "zapovest," issued in writing, if you know, how was it done when the police was planning the actions on its own?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, these were just police actions and it was not done in the same way as it is done in the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fine. So now we're on the Law on Defence, that's Exhibit P985, and I've asked you, and let me go back to my question, what do you know about the way in which anti-terrorist actions are planned and carried out in 1999?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1999 the activities designed to suppress terrorism or to carry out anti-terrorist actions was continued in the same vein as in 1998, there were no changes there. So until the order on subordination was issued, the police units would receive excerpts of the maps; and after the order on subordination was issued they would also receive the orders, "zapovesti," and the maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about Article 16 of the Law on Defence, what does it say and were you familiar with the provision at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 16 says that, "In the defence of the country the Army of Yugoslavia is the main armed force and organizer of the armed struggle, it unites all participants in the armed struggle and commands all combat activities."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right, but we did hear, didn't we, that there was certain amount of problems regarding subordination from day one, in fact. What do you know about this? Do you know what led to this misunderstanding?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know the problems concerned only one particular part of this, it concerned anti-terrorist activity, or actions if you like. There were no problems because work resumed as normal in -- as it had been done in 1998; however, at the initial stage there were a number of problems which related to varying interpretations of some legal provisions. There were differences in terms of interpretation by some officers. We from the police believed that the units to be resubordinated were those that were not involved in combat actions and that all the remaining units of the MUP should continue to go about their regular work under these new changed circumstances, and I mean the state of war that had been declared. When I say that, I mean crime control, traffic control, issuing personal identification documents, driving licences, that sort of thing. Unfortunately, as far as I know, certain members of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. On the transcript we have exactly the opposite of what you're saying. This is what it says here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, Mr. Lukic, I think we need that answer again as a simple way of doing it, and the issue is what were the differences in interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll have to repeat this. You from the police, what did you believe should be resubordinated and what gave rise to this misunderstanding, or rather, what did the army believe should be resubordinated, can you please explain that again.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. We believed, or rather, that was our interpretation of these legal provisions, that only those parts of the MUP should be resubordinated, or rather, only those units that were involved in anti-terrorist activity or in combat, if you like. And everybody else in the MUP was to carry on with their normal daily activities that they were in charge of.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just to avoid generalisations I will try to phrase my question the following way. Were there a number of officers of the VJ who believed that in addition to this police segment the non-combat segment of the police should also be resubordinated?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is precisely where problems arose initially because certain VJ officers believed that anything that belonged to the MUP and that happened to be within their area of responsibility should be resubordinated to the VJ. Just by way of an example, the entire secretariat, including the chief and the hygiene officer who was in charge of cleanliness in the secretariat building, all different lines of work; and this is the sort of problem that would happen at the outset. However, as far as I know, this was dealt with eventually and this did not affect anti-terrorist activities in any way or the defence of the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we please go back to P1996. We see that some SUP chiefs spoke at this meeting. What do we see them saying there? You've read the document, haven't you? Just go through it quickly, please.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We see the SUP chiefs speaking here and we see that they are talking about the situation in the territory of their own secretariats. The situation was quite difficult as a consequence of NATO air-strikes. We can see that a number of crimes were occurring and the secretariats were taking measures in terms of tracking down perpetrators, arresting perpetrators, filing criminal complaints. Among those, persons were civilians, active-duty policemen, reserve policemen, VJ members, all sorts of people were involved, as I say. Persons were brought in who, in addition to other crimes, had committed arson. Certain manipulations of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- of trade were prevented and so on and so forth --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, can we see what the witness is reading from?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's the whole document almost, Your Honour, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh, I see, it's not individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But this misunderstanding that he's talking about, is it dealt with here?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Misunderstanding in between police --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- and military regarding the application of the.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- law on Defence? Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we see where it's dealt with then?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Give me one minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we proceed and I -- maybe after the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I mean, the order on resubordination makes it clear it's for combat, as you know; and I would like to know more about how this -- who in the army was taking a different view.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that -- it says and MUP institutions or something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But even if that was a misunderstanding, it would be the simplest thing on earth to discuss and resolve. It's all very well to talk in these general terms, but we really need to have specific evidence about who in the army was saying that the whole MUP operation had to be resubordinated because the documents don't really give that -- give an indication that that was required.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Everyone here spends so much time emphasising the importance of cooperation among the organs of the state, in particular the VJ and the MUP, and tell us how cooperative they all were with each other. That's a prominent theme of this case. Now, how on earth do they come to have different understandings of one sentence in an order without ever actually sitting down and addressing the issue? Or perhaps they did, in which case it would be very interesting for us to hear what went on at that discussion and how it was they were able to reach agreement; or, indeed, whether there was in fact a power struggle and both sides didn't want to reach agreement or one of the two sides didn't want to reach agreement. I certainly have no clear idea of what really is the issue here at the moment, especially bearing in mind the very simple terms of that order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: As Judge Chowhan points out, if there is any question of resubordinating the whole MUP operation to the VJ, there must be a reason for that, must -- it would have to be seen to be some need. It's easy to see why the army might want resubordination of the combat units of the MUP. They have the responsibility of leading the fight to defend the country and the fight against terrorism; that's clear from Articles 16 and 17 of the Law on Defence that you've referred us to. But why on earth would they want resubordination of the traffic operations of the MUP or anything else of that nature? So it would help us to hear a bit more specific information rather than these vague generalisations about misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I've never actually explored this with this witness, but I can ask him now and I know in the future we will have some witnesses that will try to explain this issue but at the lower level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, we never discussed details, I have to say that it's my mistake because I was happy this way before I started asking you whether there were problems or not.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to explain why I think these discrepancies in terms of interpreting these legal provisions came about, and I certainly hope to be successful in this. If we look at Article 17 it reads: "In the case of imminent threat of war, a state of war, or a state of emergency, the units and organs," and I emphasise, "organs of the interior may be used for combat assignments," and so on and so forth. I don't think there's any need for me to go on reading this. This means that police units and organs can be resubordinated or may be resubordinated in the case of an imminent threat of war or in a state of war. So okay, where do I think the problem occurred in these varying interpretations? I think the stumbling block is this word, organ, because in the Ministry of the Interior there is no such thing as organs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Just the Ministry of the Interior as a whole.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- just a moment. We don't want to hear your opinion on this. No doubt, there are many opinions about what happened. What I would like to know is who in the army it was that was giving you one interpretation that didn't seem to suit the MUP, because you've told us that the misunderstanding arose in the minds of certain VJ officers who thought that everything should be resubordinated to them. Now, who were these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't involved in these conversations and I couldn't say from personal knowledge, but I did hear about what people believed. I heard my officers say what they believed as to why this had come about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what was it you heard from your officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, precisely what I was trying to explain, why the discrepancies occurred --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Precisely because their interpretation of these provisions was different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What you said just now was: "I heard my officers say what they believed as to why this had come about." Now, what had come about? That's what we're trying to understand. What was it that actually was the disagreement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure if this is an interpretation problem because I really am doing my best to explain this. I think this formulation led to the fact that varying interpretations arose. Members of the army, I don't know, maybe somebody is, but these people are not lawyers and I'm not a lawyer either. Lawyers would be best placed to explain this. But that's precisely why I was trying to say this. There was one organ, state organ, the ministry, that's the organ. Everything else are units, not organ. A secretariat is not an organ, therefore, I assume based on that, or rather, I believe that those people interpreted it like this; when they say organ they mean the secretariat so now the whole secretariat should be resubordinated. That's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand that's what you're saying as an opinion of the MUP. What I would like to know, and I think my colleagues would like to know is: Who in the army saw it differently? Who in the army was pressing you to be totally resubordinated to the VJ? Or did you just make the problem up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I didn't just make the problem up. This is something that was discussed. I'm saying I heard this from my officers. Who specifically was the commander of this brigade or another brigade, I really can't say because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that doesn't -- you can understand -- I can't fault you for that. You're frankly telling us you don't know, but you'll understand that doesn't help us in the least. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Just a minute. Now, we appreciate what you've stated, thank you very much. But of course it's a common sense question, that why army wanted to be all pervading when the requirement was less than the entire MUP falling in its folds, I mean, they could have carried on the combat things because of the inspiration given by Article 17. Why would they like everything to come under them? There must be some reason, and you are the best person to at least tell us there must have been a talk about it, there must have been a thought about it. Why would they like that, where were they so anxious to be all-pervading?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not saying that they wanted that necessarily. I don't think there was ill intention on their part, it's just this was their interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Can I just ask a question, please. I'd like to know, was there any point at -- as far as you are aware of, at which the MUP or the Ministry of the Interior sat down with the VJ and discussed this issue as to the interpretation and the different interpretation that the different sides got from it and how you could go forward from this misunderstanding as to what was the proper course or proper interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, probably yes, because I remember that I saw an order during the proofing which says precisely what I've already explained to you, that the units participating in combat should be resubordinated, whereas the other segments of the police should continue with their usual work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: But did that happen as far as you're aware?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean the implementation of the order or the discussions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Either way, what took place as far as you understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, what happened was that the activities continued as regards the anti-terrorist actions where the units of the Army of Yugoslavia continued carrying out their tasks, as in the previous period, so there were no problems, and the organizational units of the ministry and the other members of the police continued carrying out their regular tasks, their job, even in the circumstances where there was a state of war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: If your lawful action in the circumstances could only have been that a limited number of units could participate with the VJ, why did the police not just proceed in that manner? I mean, I understand the misunderstanding, but practically what would there have been to prevent you from proceeding in the manner that you could lawfully have done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, work continued, but certain military officers insisted that they take over these services that, according to law, they should not have. The police continued doing its own work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: You don't know who these officers were? Can you identify them, those who gave a different interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really cannot because I did not take part in these talks with them and I don't know who it was among them that was creating problems, I mean this kind of different interpretation. I really cannot give any names and surnames.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we've come full circle, so please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to move on to a completely different area, and I would like to ask you whether you personally or the MUP staff had information to the effect that there were paramilitary formations in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I know, no. I don't think that anyone on the staff knew that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Within the police were there any volunteers?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the police there weren't any volunteers, and that is something that the law does not allow for. The police can only have its own reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please call up in e-court 6D667.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, in this plan -- actually, let me ask you. According to this plan for marking, what units were supposed to wear ribbons?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The plan says that MUP units and VJ units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Does this document show who drafted it? Perhaps it cannot be seen.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the last paragraph underneath the table it says -- well, I conclude on the basis of that that the army drafted the document when it says: "Before setting out on a task, unit commanders must check whether soldiers and officers have replaced their ribbons in accordance with this plan," on the basis of that I can infer that it was done by the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So there was a reference to white ribbons in this table, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when ribbon colours are mentioned in the last line under number 7 it says: "White ribbon, left shoulder."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And do what do we see?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the right-hand rubric somewhere further up, in the first row it says white ribbon and in the second one it also says white ribbon on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So for the 26th, 28th, and the 31st of July, white ribbons were envisaged?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, that is what this table says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to call up in e-court 6D237, that's the document that was not translated, but I just have one question for this witness in relation to this document. I think that it's page 3 -- I beg your pardon, page 2, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't got document 237, but it have it here on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the screen.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These are instructions for wearing ribbons by the police. Just tell us the following. In this plan for the month of April, is there any reference to white ribbons?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Here it says blue, red, and yellow, those are the three colours that are used in different combinations on different days.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we just see page 6 as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the question is the same. So this is again instructions for marking the police with ribbons for June 1999. Is there any reference to white ribbons here?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, again there is a reference to blue, red, and yellow for different days.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to ask you something else. Do you know in 1999, when did the police start wearing ribbons as a form of marking? We can also have a look at another document that hasn't been translated. We can just have a look at page 1 of this document, and once it is translated we will know that it can be checked on page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Until the document -- --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Document -- untranslated document creep, I believe it's called.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, Your Honour and I --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think the witness knows the answer, anyways.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would just like to be of assistance. This first page does have a translation, it's an integral part of 4D421, this first page that Mr. Lukic is referring to, and I believe that this will be of assistance to Mr. Hannis as well, is translated within 4D421. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I would like to thank Mr. Aleksic and could we please see on e-court 4D421 now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Page 421, Mr. Aleksic, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, do you know from when the police in Kosovo and Metohija started wearing these ribbons in 1999?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this can be seen from this document dated the 15th of April, 1999, from midnight onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Do you know what the total personnel level of policemen was in Kosovo and Metohija while the KVM was in Kosovo, tentatively?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can be quite accurate because I saw these documents during the proofing, that's jogged my memory, there were 10.021 members there. This is a figure that had been agreed upon with the mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This agreement on the number of policemen, to the best of your knowledge, had it been carried out in practice as well?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because before the KVM arrived there were somewhat more policemen in Kosovo and Metohija, so this surplus personnel was returned from Kosovo and Metohija to their respective units and/or secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now let's move on to the time of war, that is to say after the 24th of March, 1999. What was the maximum number of policemen in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, before the KVM arrived we had about 14 and a half thousand policemen in Kosovo and Metohija. During the state of war, I could not be very specific, but around 15.000, up to a maximum of 16.000, I believe it wasn't more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One more question and we are going to end on that note and then we will go back to the ribbons. On the document we saw it says that at that moment the army, that is to say on the 13th of April, 1999, was not wearing ribbons, or rather, they did not have any ribbons. First of all, what was the reason, why were these ribbons introduced in the first place, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The reason for introducing these maps -- these ribbons was that -- so that the persons taking part in anti-terrorist actions could be able to recognise one another because there were cases of abuse of police uniforms. And due to that, some individuals were trapped and then kidnapped. I can give you the example of a man I new personally, Perovic was his name from the Pec SUP. That is how he got caught, they tortured him, and they killed in an abominable way. That was the reason why this was introduced, in order to protect personnel so that they could recognise each other in actions like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know in that period of time or after that period of time, since in that document dated the 25th of May that has to do with what should be worn in June, there is no such note, do you know whether the members of the army wore ribbons?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did not see that because I was not in the field and I was not following these actions; however, since this is not written in the note, I can assume that they were wearing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you don't know for yourself?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because as I've already said, I wasn't out there in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mijatovic. Those were all the questions that I had for you at this point in time. Now my colleagues will probably have some questions for you, colleagues from the Defence side and then the Prosecutor. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe, Your Honour, before we start I would have the objection to the document 5D1419 to 5D1425, it has never been released and we have never seen it, so it has never been released, it's not released yet. So we object to those documents. We object to introduction of the interview of Mr. Gajic offered by the Prosecution as I found it, because I think we had a lengthy discussion on that issue and if necessary Mr. Ivetic can be here to discuss that issue again, because Mr. Gajic gave the statement to the OTP, we asked them to be provided with this statement, we were informed that they don't have anything in writing and that the machine that recorded that interview broke and there is no any trace of that interview. Later on when Mr. Gajic died, suddenly this interview appeared. So I think if they still want to use that interview, we should have and shall have discussion on that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There was a written filing about this before?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and now we find --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But was it incidental to some other issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. I only have the instruction of Mr. Ivetic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I have a feeling it was an example of what was said to be conduct of the OTP that might have affected the admissibility of documents, and I can't remember if it was related directly to the admissibility of a Gajic document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I should point out that at this time I'm not trying to introduce the statement. It was on my notification list to documents that I might use in cross-examination, and I think that's how it came up before with a witness that Mr. Ivetic had. I was cross-examining and I listed Gajic's statement, which is P2914, as something I was going to use to ask questions from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It became part of an issue in a written filing, though. However, the point for the moment is a simple one. We encourage counsel to act the way Mr. Lukic has acted at the moment and give notice of contentious issues that may arise in the course of a cross-examination because it's very helpful to be prepared for these things when they do actually arise. So it's equally gratifying to hear from Mr. Hannis that the issue is unlikely to arise and therefore we seem to have made progress in that accidental way, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Another thing regarding 5D documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They were announced at 9.27 this morning, we didn't receive any attachment, and at that time they were not released. I don't know whether they are released yet. So we would object to these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, were you intending to cross-examine?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course, Your Honour, but I believe that I would do that after my colleagues, after Mr. Fila and Mr. Aleksic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand they are queuing up on this occasion, but the issue that's been taken about the intimation of documents which have not been released, what is the situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, those were the documents that were just found in the electronic system of the OTP, and there is probably a possibility, or rather, intention to have them used in cross-examination. I would just like to invoke the practice that we had during our Defence case and the way in which 6D presented certain documents to us then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, at least they presented them. The argument at the moment is that you haven't given them an opportunity to see the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, I did not have the possibility to see those documents until they were shown here, and even on paper and several times from the same team at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, what's being said is that this series of six documents are not in e-court, and therefore Mr. Lukic has not seen them. Now, why is that if you have them and you may be using them?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I still haven't got them, Your Honour. My colleague Mr. Lukic said that they were announced this morning and it's probably in the process of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In that case, Mr. Lukic, we will address that issue if and when it actually arises, but thank you for alerting us to it. It's now time for our break, Mr. Mijatovic, so could you again please leave the courtroom with the usher and we'll see you in half an hour, we will resume at 11.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, do you have questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Mijatovic. I hope you're strong enough to cope with me.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Let me put it this way, when this nice gentleman across the way from me will be examining you, you'll remember me with a great deal of nostalgia.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I would like to hand a hard copy of this to you. Mr. Mijatovic, yesterday you talked about the meetings that were held at the MUP staff in Pristina. One was held back in 1998 and two in 1999, and these are the two that we will be discussing. I have some documents ready for you to save your eyesight from staring at the screen that I've been staring at for the last two years and my eyesight is going. The first meeting is the meeting where you say General Obrad Stevanovic turned up as well as Djordjevic. Do you remember the chiefs of the secretariats being there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: This is 6D798 just for the record. We'll not be needing it now. Was one of the chiefs also at this meeting one called Ljubinko Cvetic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I'll ask you the way we do back in our country a direct question: Did anyone at this meeting - I'm talking about the persons who were there, Obrad and Rodja - this meeting that you said occurred on the 22nd of July, 1998, that's what the transcript reflects, did either of those two mention anything about a Joint Command being set up?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did either of those two perhaps mention that the commander of this Joint Command was Nikola Sainovic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: At page 8077, OTP Witness Ljubinko Cvetic claims that either Obrad or Rodoljub said that, that this Joint Command had been joined up, set up and that Sainovic was its commander. Do you agree with that or do you not agree?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, if someone said it, then he should know who said it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The next thing I would like to ask you is this: Can I have P1898 [as interpreted], please. You have it over there, you have a hard copy of that document. This is a meeting that was held with police leaders in Kosovo on the 4th of April, 1999. Have you found that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Was Nikola Sainovic at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, 1989, 1989.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Can you look at the document, please. I'm not sure if you've seen this one before. My first question: When you look at the introduction, the introductory part, those present, you will see that there's no reference there to Nikola Sainovic as being present?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: However, at page 4 of this record --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see page 4 in English, it's probably the same page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: -- you can see that Sainovic arrived at this meeting. Do you remember that? Do you remember Sainovic being there at the meeting? Was he there from the start of the meeting? Did he arrive later? What do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this meeting because it's obviously the case that I myself was not at the meeting. However, it's not there and I see a list of those who attended and at the beginning of the record it would certainly state that Mr. Sainovic was there. So the only conclusion that we can draw is that he came later.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Fine. Can we please now look at P1996. This is -- 1996, P1996. Have you got that? Mr. Mijatovic, have you got that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, sure. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: If -- look at this record, were you there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Was Mr. Sainovic there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and if you look at the record you can tell, both Mr. Sainovic and I were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. There's a lot there about what he said. Thank God we can all read and thank God we can all read for ourselves. There's no need for you to read it back to us, but can you please remember why he was there and what he was saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this document translated throughout or is it only the first page that's been translated?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Throughout.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's an OTP exhibit. Do you want to look at the pages, Your Honour, with Sainovic's contribution?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Not particularly, Mr. Fila, unless you want to direct our attention to them. So I was concerned that --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I'm just trying to hurry things along and I don't want to bother you with things that are not strictly necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did Sainovic stay until the very end of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Sainovic was at this meeting. He gave a speech to the SUP officers who were there, and after this meeting, after General Lukic had thanked him for participating in the work of the meeting, he was there to greet the officers and to inform of them of certain things. But then Mr. Sainovic left and the staff continued its work without Mr. Sainovic, in his absence.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Please go to pages 3 and 4 of the record. It is obvious - and I suppose you agree with me - that Sainovic was talking about this declaration by the supreme commander, this was a state directive and an order from the supreme commander. Is this something that was published in the Official Gazette, or rather, in a daily newspaper?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was published in the Politika paper, maybe in other papers too, but I knew about Politika.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Were you familiar with this communique or declaration even before Sainovic had brought it up?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we knew about this and we submitted this information to all of our units in the field, so that they might be able to acquaint their own members with this, since at the time it was very difficult to obtain any of the daily papers. There wasn't that much information going around and they were supposed to see that someone was actually following that work. It was just to keep the police officers there informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have 5D1289.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You have a hard copy of that document, sir, in front of you. Can you please have a look and tell us if this is the same thing that we have been talking about.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the article.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: First of all, whose document is this? Who produced this first page?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document by the Ministry of the Interior staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Can you look at the date, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
