utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to assist the Court. This document is in e-court and the number is P2159, unless I'm mistaken. I think we actually have a full translation of this document. My learned friend Mr. Aleksic is better informed, and I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 4D406, that's the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: As far as I can see this is a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You carry on, Mr. Fila; meanwhile, we'll try and locate it on the system as 4D406. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: As we said, this is a document produced by the staff. As far as I can see, you were the one who signed it, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I signed this on behalf of the staff leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And it has a Politika article attached to it, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So Sainovic was telling you these things, but you were already familiar with them because you had read the Politika article, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had forwarded this article on the 6th of May and Mr. Sainovic spoke on the 7th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: If you look at Sainovic's speech in that document, would the conclusion not be that actually he just -- he just told the same story that you'd read about in the papers, right, and that you already knew about?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we already knew about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that at both of these meetings that I mentioned Sainovic was at one point present, he was involved in the work of the staff, or rather, was not involved in the work of the staff in that way. He gave political speeches; that was all he did, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I'm here to defend Mr. Sainovic from very serious accusations. I'm not just swatting flies. The allegation is that at these meetings Sainovic was conveying to you directives and issuing to you orders, not giving political speeches, and it's not being alleged that he would simply come and go.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As for these speeches made by politicians, those who had been to Kosovo and Metohija, I never identified any orders or directives in whatever they said. They are speeches. They would just go there. They believed it was necessary to go there and see members of the police and the army, because these were the people defending the country, to lend them their support, and that's that. I never identified in his speeches any orders or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: This may strike you as a ridiculous question, but I'll still ask it because I have to. Was Sainovic a member of your MUP staff or was he perhaps one of the leaders in that body?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was most certainly not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You were in Kosovo both in 1998 and 1999. You know that Sainovic was the vice-president of the federal government, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did the federal government have any powers over Serbia's MUP?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The minister of the interior of the Republic of Serbia answered to the government and to the Assembly of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: All right. Another thing that a witness said here. You told us yesterday about those maps from the MUP staff. I'm not sure what I should call them, but you know what I mean, that you sent those maps to SUP chiefs?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not SUP chiefs, the commanders of those units who were involved in anti-terrorist activities. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What about SUP chiefs, did you ever send them any documents that displayed the header "Joint Command" or any reference to a Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen a document like that, nor did we ever send a document like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think you have just made it through my examination.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I hope that will continue to apply throughout.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Fila. Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: I will pick up where Mr. Fila left off just about explaining something about exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please bring back P2159, it's an e-court document. I think this is the one we are looking at our screen is 4D406, this is the English translation. P2159. There it is. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Colonel, my learned friend Mr. Fila asked you a question, you said that this was a document that you signed, of course. Can we just have paragraph 1 of this document, please, and can you read it out loud. The date is the 6th of May, 1999, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Please find enclosed an article from the Politika daily relating to the submission of reports to the president of the FRY by the head of the MUP staff in Kosovo and Metohija, Major-General Sreten Lukic, and the commander of the 3rd Army, Colonel-General Nebojsa Pavkovic. Familiarize all members of the secretariat and PJP with this article and its contents."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now can we please have 4D406 brought up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: And for you, Colonel, I actually have a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I, therefore, have the usher's assistance because the print is very small and I think you will be better able to help me with this if you actually get a hard copy to use.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: My learned friend Mr. Fila was asked you questions and in the course of his examination you said that this was the article from Politika that was at one point attached to that document of yours, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't read that, but if I look at the title I would say that it is consistent.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: If you look at the date as well, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the date too is consistent.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Colonel, second column, paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The print is very small. "While carrying out all the complex assignments, at the same time security organs," this is very small. This is too small for me to read. I can't see what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I please ask for the Serbian, the B/C/S, to remain in e-court and for us to zoom in on the central paragraph, the one in the middle. More, please, if possible -- no, no, no. The top of the page and then down the middle. Further up, please. Second column, second -- I don't know how to say this in English. Second, second, and not first. All right. Further up. Up there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Is this fine, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Can you please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I read it? "While carrying out these complex tasks security organs at the same time eliminated" -- my apologies. Again. "While carrying out these complex tasks, security organs at the same time eliminated many cases of violence, murder, theft, and other crimes whereby they arrested hundreds of perpetrators whose crimes posed a serious threat to the civilian population."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. I keep addressing you as colonel, sir, and there may be a reason for that. In your statement paragraph 1 you shared something with us about yourself, about your career. I would like to ask you one thing, though, after this secondary school of internal affairs, did you complete any other schools and which ones?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the military academy for ground forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Colonel, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please bring back Exhibit 4D421, page 1 is identical to page 1 in 6D237.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: As we have no translation for these remaining pages, I will be handing you a hard copy. We will not be discussing this a lot. I just want you to look at the totality of this document. It runs into six pages. I have a single question and we will not be dealing with any details. Colonel, sir, page 1 has been translated. You told us already who and when the ribbons and the instructions were sent to. What about page 2 and page 6, 6D237, the document in front of you, where can we find specific instructions as to how police officers should be wearing --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The object is missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: We have the plan for April in the first of these pages and the last page bears instructions in relation to the month of June. Would I be right in saying that in relation to both the instructions for April and the instructions for June there is no reference in this plan to VJ members wearing ribbons?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you look at page 6 it says instructions for the police to carry -- to wear these ribbons in June 1999, and the same thing is what we see on the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: For April, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel, sir.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just add this. We were in no position to send this to the army. We were just sending this to our own units, and this is within the police information system or reporting system. I'm not sure if the army had those or not. I don't know, really, at a later stage I mean, not April, not the first document. That's what we established. As for later, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: But you said both yesterday and today that you did not go out into the field and that you didn't know?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. My learned friend Mr. Lukic showed you 6D667 today.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please bring that up in our e-court system.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: You discussed this document with Mr. Lukic. When was the first time you saw this document, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was being proofed for my testimony here. I can't say for certain that I'd never seen it before. I simply can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. During your evidence today you mentioned something that happened in Pec which practically gave rise to these ribbons being brought over. Let me just tell you this: Witness Paunovic, who was General Lukic's first witness at transcript page 21856 repeated the same thing, said the same thing as you, as to what had given rise to this. But he also said that this was the reason, and at that transcript page he says that this was the reason that the PJP leaders devised a plan, whereas today you said --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That possibility was suggested to Mr. Paunovic and he said "maybe." He didn't express his knowledge about this issue. And exactly he answered to the question of Mr. Pavkovic's Defence. If his words could be read, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 21856.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which day --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the 7th of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I don't have the page numbers yet for the 7th of February for some reason. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 21 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's 7th February, 2007. It's 2008 we need.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 8th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2008, this year, this year, last week. In fact, it was you, Your Honour, who asked him lines 5 to 8, and the witness replied to your question in lines 9 to 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And for completeness, Your Honour, you might want to go up one more page at 21855, line 9, and there's an earlier discussion of it and the specific reference to Perovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, on the face of it Mr. Aleksic's question seems perfectly proper. Do you maintain your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Aleksic. You should put the question again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Colonel, Witness Paunovic testified and at this transcript page he said that this incident in Pec had given rise to the PJP leaders deciding that the police members should wear ribbons, and I'm asking you whether you agree with this testimony. I'm not saying that the staff made that decision.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, fine. I don't know what actually made this decision. I know that people were marked wearing ribbons. Colonel Adamovic took care of that in 1998; in 1999 it was Arsenijevic. I really can't tell you who made those plans. In 1999 it was probably Arsenijevic, and in 1998 I can't really be very specific. I don't know whether some of these plans were also made at the staff level. But from this document that we are looking at now I concluded on the basis of the title that this concerned the marking of both the police units and the army units, or rather, the personnel. And in the last paragraph it says that it should be verified whether these soldiers and officers have replaced the ribbons and that led me to conclude that this document was drafted by the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic, I'm sorry, I have no clear recollection of this from earlier. Your question was cut off by Mr. Lukic's intervention and you were contrasting what Paunovic said with what was said by this witness earlier today. And you stopped or your question was interrupted when you had said: "Whereas today you said ..." Now, what was the -- what was it the witness said earlier that you were dealing with?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely what the witness repeated. The witness said: I don't know. I may have seen this document before but I think I saw it for the first time during the proofing. But on the basis of the last paragraph the witness concluded who might have actually drafted the document. That's what the witness repeated again. And now I asked this witness who drafted that document. I had asked that of Mr. Paunovic and he had said that he didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but the conclusion he gave earlier, was his conclusion that it was drafted by the VJ or drafted by the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I now understand. Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we please have in e-court Exhibit P1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Colonel, you did say something about those meetings held at the MUP staff, not this particular meeting but some other meetings, meetings that were attended by high-ranking officials from the ministry. You answered questions asked by Mr. Lukic and by Mr. Fila. If you don't have a hard copy here in front of you, I can hand it to you. Perhaps it would be easier for you to find your way around.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would like you to do so, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: So this is a voluminous document. As far as I can see, you did attend this meeting and it was also attended by the assistant minister of the interior, General Obrad Stevanovic. What I would like you to focus on is page 6 in Serbian, which would be page 13 in the English version, where it says that people gathered there were addressed by assistant minister General Obrad Stevanovic. Colonel, I'm interested in what General Obrad Stevanovic is saying, primarily item 1, the second sentence, or rather, the second passage. Could you please read that?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Now smaller-scale actions should be organized or plan dotted closely linked actions in a number of small positions, places. Every SUP and OUP, PJP detachment, in other words, will establish a priority list of anti-terrorist actions with detailed plans which will be approved by the staff."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. In your testimony today you answered questions asked by Mr. Lukic and the Trial Chamber about the resubordination and the problems that followed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please look at item 4 on this same page in Serbian, that would be page 14 in English, to see what assistant minister General Stevanovic is saying as he addresses the PJP commanders.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The resubordination to the army should be in line with the cooperation with good information being provided from one side to another."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not have the text when we started interpreting. We start from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Resubordination to the VJ shall be in the spirit of cooperation" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just hold on until the interpreter catches up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter is reading: "Resubordination to VJ shall be in the spirit of cooperation and good exchange of information in the interest of the defence of the country and the anti-terrorist struggle ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "With the proviso that we have to know who is cooperating with the SUP and OPJP territories because a single VJ brigade can cover the territory of three SUPs so it is necessary to have all the details, to gather all the details for successful cooperation."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. The date of this document is the 11th of May, is that so?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: And these are the words of the highest-ranking MUP official both according to his rank and to his post, he's the assistant minister?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: And the decision on the resubordination or subordination, as you term it, as far as I can remember, the first decision was issued as early on the 18th or the 20th of April, if you know; if you don't, just say that you don't know.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: So almost three weeks after the decision on the subordination of the units and organs of the MUP, the highest-ranking official in the field, the assistant minister, says that the resubordination should be in the spirit of cooperation with good exchange of information. Am I right? ?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says here, that's what he said. And I was talking about the actual situation in the field. So there were no problems in the carrying out of the anti-terrorist actions, the units cooperated well, everyone commanded their units, there were problems in other parts of the ministry, the ministry parts that dealt with other tasks, not combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Colonel, sir, please do not misunderstand me. I hear what you're saying. I have no objections to your testimony. It's just that in the course of this trial we've heard other testimony and I merely wanted you to confirm what you've just confirmed, so thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I wonder if it's clear what he has confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That everyone should be in command of their own units, if I understand what the witness has said, and that the resubordination should be within the framework of cooperation and with good exchange of information. This is quite different to what some Prosecution witnesses have claimed in this trial.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may clarify, when I said that everyone was in command of their own units, that meant that if a brigade and a PJP detachment participated in an action, the detachment commander commanded his detachment and the brigade commander commanded his brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But, Mr. Aleksic, that doesn't seem to be consistent with Mr. Pavkovic's protesting that the MUP were refusing to be resubordinated in terms of that order. But you're suggesting that's -- that on the 11th of May the MUP were doing what the VJ wanted. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no, no, definitely that's not the case. The witness said that he was not in the field and that according to what he heard from his MUP colleagues, there had been some problems, but he doesn't know what was happening in the field. So I asked the witness to confirm what the assistant minister had actually said at the meeting, as the highest-ranking official in the MUP. So we're not talking about the MUP staff, we're talking about the assistant minister because we've heard testimony -- I don't want to now go through those arguments why the resubordination never happened and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What I don't understand in this is that resubordination and cooperation are two entirely different concepts, are they not?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before moving on, could we go back to page 13 again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In B/C/S that would be - just a moment, I apologise - that would be page 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Move that up to the foot of the -- thank you. Is there more at the bottom of that? No. That's fine. Just stop there. Mr. Mijatovic, there is paragraph if -- I think the B/C/S page is different, is it? Is that the same page, Mr. Aleksic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the beginning of General Stevanovic's address is at page 13 and it continues into page 14 in English, whereas in Serbian it's all on the same page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, it's paragraph number 1 on that page, Mr. Mijatovic, and you'll see reference to: "Every SUP and OPJP will establish a priority list of anti-terrorist actions with detailed plans which will be approved by the staff." What does the reference to "the staff" refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, according to what is recorded here, the secretariats were supposed to organize independently on their own those smaller-scale actions, arresting small terrorist groups, pushing them back --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, I understand that. It's -- what staff is being referred to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, probably the ministry staff because it is not specified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you're suggesting that this means that the SUPs in Kosovo had to get approval from Belgrade for minor anti-terrorist actions; is that the position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From what General Stevanovic had said, they had already received approval from the ministry leaders to organize those smaller-scale actions and for those actions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- they needed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: They needed what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They needed to draft their own plans for those activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And these were to -- and these were to be detailed plans which will be approved by the staff. Now, what staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, probably the staff of the Ministry of the Interior in Pristina but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's the MUP staff for Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The MUP staff in Kosovo. I don't know what other staff you may have been referring to, but because he was present there and because he didn't have any other address, I guess that's why he said that those plans should be submitted to the MUP staff for approval.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So does this appear to be indicating that the MUP staff for Kosovo actually does have an operational role, rather than a simple reporting function, as you indicated yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I wouldn't say that it had an operational role because the action was organized, planned, and implemented by themselves. They were in control of the action, but probably he wanted to have a look at the plans, that's probably what General Stevanovic had in mind, to perhaps make some amendments, make some suggestions regarding the plan, but it doesn't mean planning or controlling or managing those smaller-scale actions on the part of the MUP staff. That's not what it meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But it would appear to suggest that these actions could not go ahead without the approval of the MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, probably that was -- that's just the wording. The secretariats were independent, in accordance with the regulations on their organization. They carried out their tasks and work independently, but probably what this meant was Stevanovic wanted to avoid any faults, any defects in the planning phase and he wanted to go through it and perhaps make some suggestions, but this does not mean that those actions were in any way controlled or managed. It's the same way in which the commander of the Pristina Corps makes a proposal to the 3rd Army commander for some action and then he gets an approval, and then the Pristina Corps goes on to carry out this action. And the 3rd Army command does not really control or manage this operation. I'm just giving this as an example to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, my question and, no doubt, my mind is much simpler than that. I asked you if it didn't appear to suggest that these actions could not go ahead without the approval of the MUP staff. And are you saying that they could, that the SUP chief could just say, To hell with you, MUP staff, I'm going ahead with it even without your approval? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't remember. Maybe they did submit some plan, but I do not remember that a single plan was submitted to the staff --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, please treat us with a bit of respect. We're talking about the meaning of simple language, and it either means that you need the approval of the MUP staff or you don't. Are you saying to us you just don't know, there's no point in asking you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we please call up in e-court 4D101.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: I think you have that, Witness, you discussed it with my colleague Mr. Lukic yesterday. I think you have that document in front of you. You have a hard copy I believe. Do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Colonel, would you tell me when it was that you first saw this document since you said yesterday - and I agree with you - this is a document that General Pavkovic as corps commander sent to the commander of the 3rd Army personally on the 23rd of July, 1998?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw this document while I was being proofed here for giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at page 2, the last sentence there.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I read it or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. I'm just going to ask you. Am I right if I say that with this document General Pavkovic is precisely requesting what you said a few moments ago, he's asking his superior for permission to use the units of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday when you were talking to my colleague Branko Lukic about this document, you said after that on page 64, lines 12 through 19 -- well, you said that Generals Stevanovic and Djordjevic came, and you said that the two of them came in July and held a meeting at the MUP staff - and my colleague Mr. Fila mentioned that - and that they then informed you, the staff, about this adopted plan. Am I right? Is that what you were saying yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came with the intention of -- well, that meeting was attended by the representatives of the army and the police, and they came to get involved in the work of the members of the police, or rather, to take measures to have this plan materialised in concerted action with the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now call up in e-court 4D377.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: I think that you haven't got it.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: I'll give you a hard copy. This document was already shown here in this courtroom, you probably haven't seen it before. This is an order of the commander of the 3rd Army, General Samardzic, sent to General Pavkovic in the month of May 1998. And I would kindly ask you to read paragraph number 4 only of that order.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Support forces of the MUP from the deployment sector of the units using combat equipment from a distance in line with its characteristics. Provide support only following the commander," I don't know if it says "of all the MUP forces in Kosovo and Metohija and in Kosovo and Metohija, pursuant to a decision" -- now, I don't know whether this is NS, is it Chief of Staff "of the 3rd Army and commander of the Pristina Corps."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. So as far as you can see, as far as we can see, before the staff was established, the MUP staff, it has to do with the first, second, and third composition?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. Now I'm going to put some questions to you about your knowledge as to what happened specifically on the ground before that. Do you know that within the MUP during 1998 or 1999 there was a unit that was called the mechanised brigade of the police?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's the period?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: 1998 or 1999 or earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Earlier on, yes, whereas in 1998, as far as I can remember, this unit and the 24th Detachment of the PJP from Pristina together established one unit, and that was marked the 124th Intervention Brigade. As regards this document that we discussed previously, there is something that caught my attention. Support should be provided only following a request from the commander of all the MUP forces in Kosovo and Metohija. I don't know who this commander was of all these forces. There was no such person, there was no such job, but there was no commander of all forces of the MUP in Kosovo and Metohija because that would include the secretariats and the PJPs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Colonel, can you tell me whether you know how many PJP detachments were present in Kosovo and Metohija in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that at different times there was a different number involved. As far as I know, in some periods they were not complete, combinations were made, because the PJPs had A and B formations, so two companies from formation A and two companies from formation B. So I cannot give a precise answer to that because, quite simply, I was not following that at every moment how many people there were, so I mean I couldn't even remember now after all this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. I think that you already spoke about that, but I would like to ask you to repeat this. Who were they responsible to or who were they subordinated to, the PJP detachments?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every detachment is a separate unit and was headed by its commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: And this commander of the detachment issued tasks and commanded the detachment in combat activities?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already explained that. On the basis of the documents received from the Pristina Corps, he organized the work of his unit in these activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: But yesterday you said - as far as I can remember you repeated it today as well - that from the corps you only received excerpts from maps -- no, sorry, not you, they received it.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1998 until resubordination took place -- I mean, I'm saying "subordination" because that is what the law says, it's the same sense, the same meaning, subordination, resubordination, but that's what the law says. So when I said about these orders, "naradjenje" "naredba," subordination, they received maps and later on they would get orders, "zapovesti," and maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic, is your question who gave orders to the PJP? Can you answer that question, please, Mr. Mijatovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that it? I'll repeat once again. Anti-terrorist activities were taking place in 1998 on the basis of a plan that was adopted at top state level envisaging the participation of police units and army units. The Pristina Corps planned these activities for the units of the police as well. That plan was their basis for conducting this planning, so it involved the police units too, they submitted excerpts of maps, and that was the basis for action on the part of PJP detachments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: They had to obey the Pristina Corps; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was their basis. That was the basis for the commanders, the documents prepared by the Pristina Corps for them to organize the work of their units, and they had control over their units. I'm not saying that directly the Pristina Corps commanded them in these activities or am I saying that I know who brought together these activities in the field, from what particular place and who personally did that, which commander or officer. I was not there, I was not in the field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's say they didn't turn up - we've had some evidence of that on at least one occasion - who would they be answerable to? Who would take action against the PJP unit for disobedience?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot recall any such situations, although that I -- although I did hear that there was mention of something like that here in this courtroom. As far as I know, there were no such problems and all of that was resolved directly in the field between the two commanders --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, indulge me for a moment and just imagine that that might happen. Take the hypothetical situation where it does. Who would that -- who would be -- who would it be who would take action to discipline the unit which did not turn up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The staff did not have the authority to take disciplinary measures; I said that yesterday. It did not have that authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Nor did I. What I want to know is who did.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Disciplinary measures vis-a-vis detachments of the PJPs could be taken by their officers from the original secretariat that they had been sent from. Say a detachment from Nis had been sent, they did something they were not supposed to do, it is their officer, their ranking officer, from the secretariat that will take disciplinary action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Colonel, in relation to what you said just now, you said that disciplinary punishment would be meted out against the members of the PJP detachment by the head of their original SUP. What about PJP commanders, is the chief of the original SUP in charge of him too or the SUP that they were sent to as assistants?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander just like any other policeman from the PJP belongs to a certain secretariat and is an employee of that secretariat, and if there are disciplinary infractions then it is the chief of the mentioned secretariat that will take action.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification, Colonel. Since you said that you graduated from the military academy of land forces of the army, do you personally know that combat orders can be issued in writing and orally?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, as far as I know, the army does it in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: What about lower levels?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at a lower level, it is possible to do it orally. For instance, the platoon commander would issue his orders orally to squad leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Colonel, do you know that combat orders for units are made two levels down, in other words, army commander would issue orders to the corps and combat group level. I don't know whether you know that from your military education.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not contesting that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Now I have to go back to something. You mentioned a plan, that the plan was the basis for this. Let us not go back to it, but you said yesterday that this plan was never received by the staff and that you actually had never seen it, if I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did not see it and I assume that I would have seen it had it come to the staff. I didn't see it, we didn't have it at the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please confirm once again, you said that you did not attend any of the meetings where any plans were adopted at that scale?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're talking about the basic plan? No, no, that was done in Belgrade at the level of the president of the state. I was not invited and I didn't feel any need to be involved in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. This was -- this completes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, you have cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, good afternoon. My name is Djuro Cepic. I'm representing General Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Colonel, I will pick up where my colleague Mr. Aleksic left off. We were talking about a plan in a document you read yesterday that this plan was dated the 9th of June; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So what was the date of that plan?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the decision taken at the Supreme Defence Council, that was taken on the 9th of June. The plan itself was made, according to what we learned from the documents, in the first half of July. And on the 21st of July it was adopted by the president of the republic, Mr. Milosevic, that's what it says in the document of the Pristina Corps sent to the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: When was the first time that you saw this document from the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was preparing for my -- for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The decision is dated the 9th of June; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No -- oh, yes, no, the decision, I'm sorry, yes, the decision to draft this plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have Exhibit P1505.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And while we're waiting for this document to come up on our screens, I think you have the hard copy in front of you, this is the decision to establish the ministry staff. In your testimony yesterday you said at page 53 of the transcript that the minister of the interior could have taken part in taking this decision, and in fact that he did so, the minister of the Republic of Serbia. Who was it at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was Vlajko Stojiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we please look at the document on this -- on the date on this document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 16th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: How many days after the 9th of June is it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's seven days.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, could you please look at the last page in this document. Who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vlajko Stojiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He issued this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Colonel, in your evidence yesterday you said something that you confirmed again today. You said that you had never seen the plan to suppress terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we please look at 6D798.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I would like to show it to you. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what is the date on this document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 22nd of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We see here in the preamble the persons who actually attended the meeting, and we can see that you were present, all the SUP chiefs, all the commanders of the PJP detachments, the Generals Djordjevic, Stevanovic, and others. Do you remember this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at paragraph 3 or, more specifically, I would like you to read it to see whether the translation is correct.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Determining the tasks in relation to the implementation of the global plan and further tasks -- and further task."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, could you please explain to me what is the global plan?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether this plan that was adopted on the 21st of July at Mr. -- at President Milosevic's place, whether it was entitled the global plan or whether somebody used this phrase and it was recorded by the recording clerk, I can't say that, but the reference here is definitely to that plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this clarification --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, you're -- by this time you're number two in the MUP staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: General Lukic is number one and he's proposing --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- an agenda and one of the items is defining tasks in the implementation of the global plan. Are you saying to us that you as number two do not know what he was talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm saying that there may be -- may have been a slip of the tongue or maybe the person -- the recording clerk made a mistake. Now, whether this plan had this title or not, I don't know. The only thing I know is that this was the plan that was devised to suppress or to fight terrorism. Perhaps that was its title. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, we've become increasingly concerned about the extent to which you are actually complying or attempting to comply, rather, with the terms of the solemn undertaking you gave us to give us the whole truth. We have power to take action in respect of witnesses that we consider are not endeavouring to comply with the terms of the solemn undertaking they gave. I warn you of that power now. I ask you to reflect upon the answers that you've been giving so far, in spite of our earlier warning to you that you ought to treat us with some respect and recognise that we are individuals endowed with common sense. We're going to break now for our lunch break, which will be for one hour. I hope that that will give you time to reflect upon the obligation you have to make full disclosure of your personal knowledge to this Trial Chamber. Would you now please leave the courtroom with the usher and we will see you again in one hour's time at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.42 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I kindly ask you to listen to me for a few moments. Maybe it's my mistake that I didn't have the document to show to this witness, and trust me, this Defence would love to have that document. I think that the Prosecution also tried to find the document. My explicit instruction to this witness was, as to any other of our witnesses, is not to guess, just to tell you what he knows. And as you know, during this trial we used three different names for that plan. Our Defence does not know the name of that document. We just found --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, would you leave the courtroom, please, with the usher while I listen to what Mr. Lukic has to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you could hear from this witness, he never saw the document. He confirmed the contents, he confirmed that that's that plan, but he never knew the real name. He never said that he was not aware of the plan. He said that he does not know the exact name, and trust me this Defence does not know that name. And I'm sure that the Prosecution cannot tell you the exact name of the document because we are finding three different names for that document during this trial. So actually, I told you a few moments, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The question which was asked, Mr. Lukic, that started this particular exchange, although what I said was not confined to this: "Could you please explain to me what is the global plan?" Now, he was at a meeting where Major-General Sreten Lukic, head of the MUP staff in Pristina is recorded in minutes, which are MUP minutes, as defining tasks in the implementation of the global plan and the following task. And his answer to that question was: "I don't know whether this plan that was adopted on the 21st, whether it was entitled the global plan or whether somebody used this phrase. I can't say that, but the reference here is definitely to that plan."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly. He does not know the name and he knows that it's actually that plan. We used the term global plan, we used the term five-phase plan, and we used the term plan for the combat against terrorism. And we don't know the exact name. So he does not know if it's really global plan. And you can see that the witness said: "But the reference here is definitely to that plan," so he was -- he only couldn't give you the name of the plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'll give him an opportunity when he comes back in to amplify that answer before we proceed further with Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before he enters, sorry, one thing. Mr. Mijatovic really put a great deal of effort to go through as much as possible of our documents. He read a lot. The fact is that at that time he couldn't recognise some of the documents, he didn't remember, and he really tried to prepare himself as much as possible. And trust me, he was our -- the most diligent witness we have. So it's not that he didn't try to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your experience --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- familiarize himself with everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but your experience in preparing witnesses is not a matter for us--

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- to have regard to, Mr. Lukic. We will judge the witnesses according to what they say in court and all the evidence that might have a bearing on what they say in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But what I'm trying to tell you, he really tried to prepare himself, and some things he wouldn't be able to give you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We'll allow him the opportunity to explain whatever he wants to explain and we'll take account of the whole circumstances surrounding his evidence. That's all we can do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, in the document which is on the screen, there is reference to the agenda proposed by General Lukic, and the third item is: "Defining tasks in the implementation of the global plan and the following task." Now, can you tell us in general the nature of the plan, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me say this again. I didn't see the plan, I didn't see the substance of that plan, I didn't read it. But what was mentioned was that police units should work with the VJ and be involved in those activities, that they should prepare for that, and that they would be given, as I said, more specific tasks in relation to each action. That is what I remember globally speaking. I can't remember every single word that was said, needless to say, but they were saying that the units should prepare for the execution of those tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, sir, let's pick up where we left off.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have P1991 brought up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, can you see the header of this document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What's this about? What is this document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a record from the meeting of the staff with the minister of interior of the Republic of Serbia, the chiefs of the secretariats from Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And the date?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 21st of December, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We see a list of those who attended the meeting, we see your name there. You were there, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What about the previous meeting and this meeting and all these other meetings, not a single VJ person was there, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at this one, not at the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go to page 2 of the B/C/S, it's page 3 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Please look at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the last paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, where you see Obrad Stevanovic, I'm just looking at the English to find the reference. It should be page 3 -- page 4. Can you please read this paragraph Lieutenant-Colonel-General Obrad Stevanovic asked the --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "SUP chiefs to report briefly on how plans to combat terrorism were being implemented and to" --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That will do. Will you please tell us what plans these would be?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What he probably had in mind was individual plans in relation to the fundamental plan, individual plans and activities in individual anti-terrorist actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You mean plans up until the month of October, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me this, these plans were done only in the MUP, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that it was based on that fundamental plan or basic plan that the Pristina Corps made specific plans for specific actions, and the MUP was receiving map extracts for their own units.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is that your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yesterday and today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Shown the time-period for which he is testifying. I'm not aware if he saw the date and if he thinks it's something during the summer of 19 -- he should get a time-frame.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may, my previous question was about the time-period of all things, and the witness confirmed that these were plans up until the month of October 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We're still on the same page. Can we please go to the last paragraph on that page. In the Serbian this is page 4. Do you remember who Bosko Petric was?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the chief of the Pristina SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please just go to the previous page, go back to the previous page in the B/C/S, it's page 3, the top of the page. We have it in the English. Here, have a look, the top of the page says Bosko Petric briefly said that a plan was drawn up to combat terrorism and for the most part it was being implemented. Can you tell me this was a special MUP plan that the Pristina secretariat produced for their own purposes?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the secretariat had the task of producing their own plans for combatting terrorism; however, combatting terrorism did not just imply individual actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: If I may, Colonel, just to hurry things along a little, this is the only thing I want to know. These are plans that were done by the MUP alone, a MUP body, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were plans that were made by the secretariats, but it's not about combat action of that kind only. There are a number of things one can do, gathering intelligence on terrorist groups, on individuals, on their whereabouts, on arresting them, and so on and so forth. So these are the plans that this refers to, the plans made by the secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And these plans made by the secretariats, this was something that was the responsibility of the MUP and MUP alone?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The secretariats alone, sole responsibility?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say that there wasn't a local action, for example, where a group needed to be blocked and crushed, I can't say that the army was not involved, but this was not a plan that was produced by the corps or the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I see. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because these are local actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You remember the incident, I assume, in December 1998 when a number of young men came to grief in the Panda cafe in Pec?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: After that brazen terrorist attack a MUP unit stepped in and conducted a legitimate action to track down terrorists in the village of Kapesnica, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember which secretariat, when and how implemented those small-scale actions. I can't enter into any details here. On the other hand, sure, they were working on combatting terrorism and there were situations like that, but I can't remember any specific details simply because I never saw their plans, I don't know where it was that they carried them out. Maybe there were results mentioned in one of the reports, I do allow for that, but I can't remember the name or the date or where these actions were carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Of course you were receiving reports from all the detachments of the secretariat of the interior, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I spoke about that yesterday. We were receiving daily, regular, and interim reports from the secretariat. The detachments in the course of an action -- I don't know who exactly they would be reporting to, and if they were, I wasn't there, I wasn't out in the field, I was in no position to monitor exactly what was going on and how they went about that. After the completion of the anti-terrorist action, members of the detachment were under an obligation to inform the local secretariat about any occurrence or development that the secretariat would have had to act on. It was sometimes the case that detachment commanders would inform the MUP staff as well about the individual developments or if they had come up against a problem. For example, they'd suffered losses, an action was aborted for some reason, an action was never even launched, there were people who were wounded, they needed help getting them to the hospital, they needed beds to be made available at a hospital, perhaps some other kind of problem, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All right. This explains it at a lower level. So these were small-scale actions and these were planned by the SUPs. Tell me about actions of a broader scope in terms of anti-terrorist actions, who was it that was planning these actions?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, such large-scale actions were based on the plan to combat terrorism, and this is a plan that we had been referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So who did the planning on behalf of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, extract maps for police units that were involved in those actions were provided by the Pristina Corps. It was based on this that unit commanders of both the military and the police would coordinate their activities. The police commander was in charge of his unit, commanded his unit, the army commander commanded his unit, they coordinated their activities and actions were carried out. At least that's as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Maybe what I'm about to say next will jog your memory a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like page 6 in B/C/S to be displayed of this same document that's in front of us; in English page 10, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So it's this same meeting when you were present. You see the heading here. As I'm going down one, two, three, four, five, the fifth bullet point, "Broader actions towards terrorist bases," could you please read that out?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Broader actions towards terrorist bases should be planned by the ministry staff; however, the initiative should be with the secretariats who should make preparations and compile recommendations of the activity plan. All these plans should be based on the principles of a police operation."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mijatovic, you attended this meeting, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And these are the words of Obrad Stevanovic, General Obrad Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And you do not remember that the MUP in Pec and other places carried out independent actions?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot talk about plans and the timing involved, but they did carry out actions, yes. That is within the plan of the general combat against terrorism. What I explained a few moments ago, what it all -- what it includes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Colonel, you probably know that up until the beginning of the war, or rather, the aggression against our country, the main task of the units of the Army of Yugoslavia, or rather, of the Pristina Corps was the protection of the state border from the spillover of terrorism from the Republic of Albania and Republic of Macedonia; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what period are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Up until the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And 1998 too, the basic tasks.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what the tasks of the army were. I didn't read their orders, but the army is the one that defends the border. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So therefore you do not know how the use of fire and fire support were approved to be given by the army to the MUP in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how it was approved, down what chain it went, but I know that both units took part in that struggle, or rather, in these anti-terrorist actions on the basis of that plan. And now what the procedure was, who wrote what to who, that, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Now I am going to deal with the summer of 1998 and the activities in suppressing terrorism in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija during a period of a bit over two months. Tell me, Lieutenant-Colonel Adamovic, was he operationally in charge of the MUP actions from the MUP staff in 1998?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1998 Adamovic did -- was not in charge of anyone in the MUP, he was a member of the staff in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What was his duty?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in charge of operational affairs in the staff, partly he worked on logistics, too, for the units and secretariats. He participated in providing information, or rather, he provided information for the planning of anti-terrorist activities to the Pristina Corps, he knew where the units were, he followed that, he followed the problems they had, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Was he a military academy graduate?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Who decided what MUP units would be?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: For particular tasks.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on the territory involved of secretariats, say Kosovska Mitrovica or Prizren, then Adamovic knew what unit was there and that that unit could then be used; however, it wasn't logical if the action was taking place in the territory of Pec to send a PJP from Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: For example, we have a problem in Mitrovica, and Adamovic thinks that it is necessary to involve not only the local PJP company from Mitrovica but also the PJP detachment. How does he decide which detachment is supposed to take part in this action?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he's not the one who decides. He's the one who provides information what units are there in the area and which units can be used. He cannot give information that a unit from Prizren can be used in the territory -- if activities are taking place in Kosovska Mitrovica and there is a detachment there already. There is no need for him to give information for Prizren, there is nothing for him to decide there. The unit is already in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Who knows where the MUP units are in the area? Who has this information?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we know that on the basis of the order on mobilisation from the dispatch that came to the staff from the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: When did that dispatch arrive?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For every shift a separate one would arrive for every mobilisation and every send-off. Everyone knew what unit was sent to the territory of what secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Who in the Ministry of the Interior issues this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister or one of his co-workers whom he authorises.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Who tours and inspects PJP units in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of inspection you're talking about. I know that I did not go out into the field, but I know when Generals Djordjevic and Stevanovic were there they often went out into the field, but what they did, what their tasks were, I really don't know. We did not inspect the PJP in any way, we, the members of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The detachments and secretariats, who did they send their reports to in the MUP once an action was over?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once an action was over, the detachments - and I've already said this - informed the secretariat about certain events regarding which the secretariat is supposed to take measures. When the secretariat acts in relation to such and such an event, they compile a daily report, including all other events, including that event that was reported by members of the PJP. And then the SUP took action with regard to that, as they did in respect of any other action. And this daily report was submitted to the Ministry of the Interior and to the staff, along parallel lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, if an action by a PJP detachment goes well and there's nothing to be done at the end of it, does that mean there would be no obligation to report anything to the SUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the commander of the detachment or the officer leading the detachment during that task quite simply provides information that the action was over, that there were no problems, and that there is no -- that there are no elements upon which the secretariat should act. However, since logistically the detachments relied on the secretariats in terms of being provided with food, water, fuel, accommodation, and so on, they were always in contact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So does it come to this, that there always was a report from the detachment to the SUP about their activity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, he did not submit some kind of detailed reports to the SUP, like what the military does, but he would inform that the task was over, that he needed fuel, lubricants, spare parts for a damaged vehicle, and so on. So since they needed logistics support from them, they were always in contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in the MUP of the Republic of Serbia there is, or rather, there was a set of instructions on the way in which internal affairs will be regulated in the security sector?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm aware of these instructions, and as for these plans --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Intervene for the transcript, I believe at page 86, line 19, the witness said in Serbian "borbeni izvjestaji," combat reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic, there seems to be an incomplete answer to your question at line 24. Do you want to pose the question again or are you content with what you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Let's just go back to this, Colonel. The entire answer was not recorded in the transcript, so I'm going to put the same question to you yet again. Do you know that in the MUP there are instructions on the way in which internal affairs are set up and organized in the security sector?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are such instructions, but whether that is the exact name I cannot say, but there are instructions for measures to be taken in this sector, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that inter alia these instructions say that every police station in its dossier inter alia has to have a list of members of special police units, an in-depth plan of border security, a plan of blockade of the area of the station, and other things?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite frank, I was not involved in that particular line of work; and as for all the things that the dossier of this sector should include, I really cannot say. I was never commander or "komandir" of a police station, I was never head of a sector, I did not apply these instructions, so I really cannot talk about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, but you graduated from the military academy, like part of your superior officers, like General Obrad Stevanovic and others; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this was not studied at the academy. This is pure police work.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In addition to your superior officers and the officers who were commanders of the PJPs, almost all of them had graduated from the military academy; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The one from Nis -- Mitrovic, Mitrovic, not; but Zivaljevic Grekulevic, Prljevic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Zivaljevic. Grekulevic I think the answer is yes; Prljevic yes; I don't know about Stalevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What about Brakovic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Bosko Buha?
