utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's to the best of my knowledge. No, I mean I don't know what the man graduated in, but as far as I know was in the academy.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Josipovic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot say about him either.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Zinajic?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I cannot say what kind of school he finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We can agree that most of them had graduated from military academies?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't do any counting like that and I cannot really say something like that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yesterday and today you confirmed to us that you got excerpts from maps from the corps and you passed that further on to PJP detachments. In these excerpts one could not see the specific tasks of companies. It was only PJP detachments that were marked, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't really pay much attention to these details, but it is logical that if there is an excerpt in terms of how a unit should act, one should be able to see the lower-ranking units there too, for as I know, for two ranks down. If a plan is made on a map, if one provides the deployment of the units, then as far as I know, it's done at two ranks below as well. Perhaps I may have forgotten by now, but you cannot have the detachment without the other units. You have the axis of movement, the point of departure, the line to which they should come, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: However, today you don't remember exactly what was marked there, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've been saying that I did not see this in any detail. Other people did that. I saw these excerpts for units, I mean I saw people coming there to take that. But I know in principle what this should contain. I do not rule out the possibility of having glanced at some of them, but what particular units or detachments were involved, I really cannot say. But for every unit when a task is given on the map excerpts, one has to see the point of departure, the axis of activity, the line that they should reach, and also, as I said, on the basis of that, the commander of the detachment would elaborate his own task with his lower-ranking officers. That is only natural. That is what any unit does. Now, whether he drew maps there, wrote orders, "zapovesti," or not, that I don't know. As far as I know, they did not have the technical capacities to do that out in the field, but I don't rule out the possibility that they were perhaps involved in some schematics.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So the detachment commander issues an order to company commanders in a written form or verbally, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, those are his subordinate officers, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: PJP company commanders issue orders to platoon commanders; that's the next step, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a platoon commander must know where he's going, with what unit, what the axis is, what direction, they must know all these things. It's only natural and it's only logical to expect them to know this. This is a natural thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All right. Explain this. There's the map extract. There is no signature, no stamp, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. As I said, I didn't make those myself, I didn't study them in detail, I didn't adopt those, I didn't deliver those, submit those; other people did that, but I know that those came and I know based on what the police units took action. Therefore, I can't go into any detail on this since I wasn't paying attention and I wasn't looking at details.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you not allow for the following possibility, marked on an extract we see the 35th Detachment. Instead of the 35th, the 122nd Intervention Brigade turns up.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't possibly comment on that. I was not aware of any such a situation and I don't know what you're talking about. There is no logic to it. If one unit is planned, that unit, then Adamovic says that the unit can participate; and now instead of that unit you have a different unit turning up with no replanning, no amendments to the plan, I don't know. It's not that I can't allow for that possibility. I simply don't know whether that was, in fact, done in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Let's assume this sort of situation occurs. You have a map extract saying the 35th, the 35th PJP Detachment, and yet on the ground instead of the 35th PJP Detachment, the 122nd Intervention Brigade shows up. Who decides this?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can't simply show up unless they received a map extract first.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You are claiming that, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not claiming that, but I don't know if it's possible for a detachment to go off on a mission if no mission has been received.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that PJP detachment commanders issue orders to their subordinates, the subordinates in turn issue orders to their subordinates, and so on and so forth. How does this chain work? Who would sign a decision map for a company commander, for a detachment commander?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A detachment commander -- I don't know how many times I've said this already.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We know that. I'm not asking you that. Answer this specific question. Who signs a decision for the MUP forces and is a decision like that signed?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no such decision in the staff because the detachments that were involved were involved based on map extracts obtained from the Pristina Corps for their use, for their involvement. No decision was made by anyone else or signed on behalf of -- for detachment commanders as far as the staff was concerned or the MUP generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So it is your evidence that they would go into actions where you were not familiar with any orders or any signatures; one simply took action on the ground. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what I was saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You're an educated person, you're a graduate of the military academy. You probably know that once an order, "zapovest," is received and a decision on a map, this is a mere basis, this is groundwork, and one must produce one's own order based on those, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the detachment got extracts. Did the detachment commander make an order, did the company commanders make their orders, I don't know. I wasn't on the ground, I wasn't there, I couldn't see, I couldn't, as they say, verify that. Maybe they did, maybe they didn't; the thing is I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: All right. This detachment commander must do something else for his subordinates. He must draft a decision map for two levels of command down, and this map must then be approved by his superior officer, is that right, is that the procedure? So your evidence is you don't know what must be done?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is probably the system used by the army, but it's not the one used by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can we therefore conclude that the systems used by the police on the one hand and the army on the other were to a high degree different?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure to what degree, but this happens to be one of the differences, the one that we just discussed. Secondly, after an action has been completed army units submit detailed combat reports and this did not apply to PJP detachments. My apologies to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, when these maps were sent by PJP -- sorry, by the Pristina Corps, were they always channelled through the detachment commander or were such reports issued directly by the Pristina corps to company commanders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think, I can't say for sure, but I don't think company commanders but detachment commanders, but I can't say because I didn't do that, so I'm not sure how many maps there were. Such maps, but PJP detachments, yes, and based on this the detachment commander could then plan an order for his units; but I can't rule out the possibility that these were issued in relation to companies as well. It's just that I'm not in a position to claim that with certain knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you know for sure that these extract maps were, in fact, sent to detachment commanders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, they certainly weren't held back in the staff. Once Arsenijevic got this or later he would forward this to the units, because the unit could not go into action without something like this because this is the basic document on which they base their work, this is the initial document, if you like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I think I had missed that evidence earlier. These were sent by the Pristina Corps to the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the needs of PJP units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You referred there to Arsenijevic, but a bit earlier in your evidence you were asked about Lieutenant-Colonel Adamovic, I think. These extracts always went through Arsenijevic, did they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That went through Adamovic, through Adamovic for as long as he was there. He was there in 1998 and early 1999, up until the beginning of the air-strikes, and then he was hit during the air-strikes and was sent back to the ministry and was replaced by Arsenijevic. Arsenijevic was the man who replaced him on this job. Therefore, these two persons were involved, one at an earlier stage and the other at a later stage. I'm sure they would be in a position to provide a lot more detail on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, it was your understanding that these documents had gone to the MUP staff, was it? That was the evidence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That wasn't my understanding and I certainly don't accept that; however, I do have a number of questions remaining that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Has there been evidence so far in the course of his evidence that you recollect to that effect?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it was mentioned in chief. He spoke about the extracts, and I think Mr. Lukic was examining the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And the evidence was that these were sent to the MUP staff for Kosovo; is that the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can just intervene, I didn't want to interrupt the exchange, but at page 93, line 4, again it was reports is in the transcript but the witness said combat reports, "borbeni izvjestaji," in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, can we continue?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You're a graduate of the military academy, your experience is considerable. In view of that, you'll probably agree with what I'm about to suggest next. Were someone from MUP to receive a map extract like that, this would constitute a basis for coordination and for concerted action and it would facilitate the work of the MUP detachment in question in terms of being better able to more efficiently plan their commitments and activities, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I've been saying so far. This is something that was for detachment commanders as a basis which they could then use to plan units [as interpreted] for their own subordinate units; likewise, another commitment would be to establish coordination and cooperation with a VJ unit commander to link up to plan this together and in an action each would be in charge of their own respective units. I've said this a number of times, haven't I?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And the chains of command are entirely separate, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within units, yes, because everyone's in charge of their own unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Of course you know that a map, as such - and this is something that you testified about - must follow a written order. It's not an independent document, a stand-alone document, is it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you what we got, I'm telling you what we forwarded to our units; what it should be or must be is a different issue altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You spoke yesterday about subordination and you said that following an order on resubordination -- on subordination you would receive orders and maps, but not up until that point in time. This was the second half of April, right, 1999?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was from the time the order on resubordination was adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any order whatsoever from the interior minister regarding subordination?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The VJ?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, you, the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but did we get an order from the minister to resubordinate MUP units to the VJ?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, at least none that I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What about the MUP staff or anyone from the Pristina MUP, did they issue to anyone an order, as in "naradjenje," or an order as in "zapovest," on subordination. Was any order, as in "naradjenje," issued to any detachment, any SUP, any police station?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not as far as I know. I don't think anybody could have done that without the minister, bypassing the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Correct me if I'm wrong, yesterday you said that organs of the interior, secretariats of the interior, you explained about the department of the interior, you explained about the police stations, are these organs of the interior?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What are they then?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are organizational units of the Ministry of the Interior. The Ministry of the Interior is an organ, it's a state organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Fine. All right. One thing you didn't say is what PJP units were.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are not organizational units of the ministry under the organization rules; these are set up by a special decision taken by the minister. And they operate, and I hope you know this, on the principle of being assembled. When there's a need, then people from organizational units from the ministry are taken away from their regular duties, a unit is set up and then sent on a mission, and that's why it's no organizational unit within the ministry, the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: SAJ and JSO, what about those?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: SAJ is within the state security sector and I can't discuss that, I simply don't know -- or rather, the JSO is. The SAJ, on the other hand, as far as I remember, was established pursuant to an -- to a decision by the minister, but it was a permanent set-up, a permanent unit. At one point in time it was an organizational unit of the ministry, I think it still is but I can't say because it's been a long time since I last looked at the rules. It's a permanent set-up, it's a permanent unit and it doesn't do anything else but their own jobs. Members of the PJP also police and patrol certain areas, their stations commanders and assistants and so on and so forth. Therefore, this is the manpower that is used to set up a PJP along the principle of actually assembling them and pursuant to a decision by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we show an error in the transcript, page 97, line 22, not SAJ but JSO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: First word -- okay. Thank you. I just received information from my colleagues that there's a correction at the end of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, the point that I would make out is that that's not what the witness said. The "or rather the JSO" is the interpreter's comment I believe, because the witness was rather clear, as Mr. Cepic points out, when answering the question that he was talking about the JSO from the onset. So we need to have a clear delineation between comments of the translators and what witnesses are actually saying. Mr. Cepic is correct in bringing this error in denomination to the attention of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The JSO is the one that's within the state security sector. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you're asking me, then the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you claim, Mr. Ivetic, that line -- page 97, line 23 onwards is about the JSO?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I claim that the statement, "Or rather, the JSO is ..." is the interpreter's correction, not what the witness said. The witness started the sentence saying: "The JSO is within the state security sector," in line 22 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: He said, "I can't discuss that, I simply don't know." And then that's where his answer about the JSO ends and the translator clarifies the error earlier translation I believe. We can always have that clarified by listening to the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think that's clear. Carry on, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Colonel, the OPG, RPO --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go ahead, ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: OPG, RPOs, what kind of formations are we talking about, are they permanent? Are they temporary?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the RPO is concerned, that's the reserve police departments, they were established before my arrival in Kosovo and Metohija and they are composed of the reservists in the Ministry of the Interior, or rather, the police and the reserve force of the Territorial Defence units. These are temporary formations, and the reason why they were established was to provide security to the civilian population in built-up areas to protect them against terrorist acts. As far as the OPG units are concerned, the OPG members are active staff of the ministry, and when we're talking about Kosovo and Metohija those formations were established sometime in late 1998, I believe, and they had 10 to 15 men, maybe up to 20, they differed in size I think but their strength would be something like that. And they comprised members of the PJP units from the secretariats in Kosovo and Metohija. The reason why they were set up was because in that period - and actually you yourself mentioned the attack on the Panda cafe in Pec - the reason was because the terrorist acts started to be carried out in urban areas, and this posed a threat to the security in urban areas. And in order to prevent any large-scale consequences, those operational pursuit groups were established.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yeah, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can give you the whole genesis of the very name, it hails back to 1970s --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've more than answered the question. Mr. Cepic, can we concentrate on what's in controversy.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your testimony yesterday, Colonel, you did not mention those formations. Am I right when I say that the JSO and the SAJ and the PJP and the OPG are the manoeuvre component of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is a difference when it comes to PJP. First of all, OPGs are part of the PJP --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you please just give me short answers so that we can move through my questions fairly quickly. Can you tell me, is this the manoeuvre segment of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are manoeuvre detachments, and not all detachments are manoeuvre detachments. There are those detachments, but not all of them are of that nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The A variant of the PJP, SAJ, OPG, that would be the manoeuvre detachments?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the A variant.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So all the detachments, all the formations that I mentioned, they belong to that set?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In addition, each SUP had its own PJP units; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the PJP units were part of the secretariats, regardless of where they were in Serbia, whether in Kosovo and Metohija, in Vojvodina, or in Serbia proper. So all PJP members were at the same time members of one of the secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, but in action we can see that a PJP company from Urosevac would take part and some detachment from Nis or from the Serbian hinterland, just to give you an example?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't see where the problem is. A detachment was formed from units from several secretariats. One secretariat would give one company, the other one would give, let's say, four companies, depending on their capabilities and strengths. So that in the Nis detachment not all of the personnel would be from Nis or Uzice or Novi Sad. For example, the Novi Sad company would comprise personnel --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Let's stop there. We're making this too broad.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do apologise. I just wanted to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Am I right when I say that the combat control of the territory, securing roads, axes and facilities and features, were also part of combat activities that those units carried out, further blocking certain areas, setting up ambushes, raids, and other tactical actions?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't be talking about combat control of the territory because it is a military term, that is not a police term. But definitely the police units did control the roads, the territory; after all, it is its task to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you attend any meetings attended by the MUP leaders and the Army of Yugoslavia officers except for the one in the summer of 1998?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of meetings you're talking about of the same kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember any official meetings, but there would be coordination, cooperation, but meetings of that kind as the one that we discussed at the beginning, the anti-terrorist activities, I can't recall any meetings of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, who do you report to when a policeman is killed?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, the staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The staff and the unit from which this policeman was.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if the policeman is killed and he belongs to a certain detachment, then the secretariat and the staff get a report, and that would be the urgent report that we were talking about, and the secretariat then puts it into its daily report. There is an on-site investigation, if possible, the public prosecutor is told about that and so is investigative judge --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Okay, okay.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do apologise. And the ministry also receives a report through regular reporting channels and so does the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Who provides the food, ammunition, and all the other necessary things for MUP units?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I've already said, from the point of view of logistics the detachments relied on the secretariats in the territory. When they came to carry out the tasks they brought all the ammunition they needed with them, but if it happened that more ammunition is expended than was expected, then additional quantities were procured through the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I intervene for the transcript. It might be due to the intervention of Mr. Cepic in the middle of that answer which broke up the answer, but lines 6 and 7 at page 103 do not accurately reflect what the witness said. I don't know whether it's best to just have that listened to, the tape, but we understood the witness to say that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, you were being asked about reports and you said there was an on-site investigation, if possible, the prosecutor is told, so is the investigative judge, and then you went on to say who else received reports through regular reporting channels. Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The secretariat that covered the territory in question undertook measures within its jurisdiction to process the incident. The investigative judge and the public prosecutor were notified, an on-site investigation was carried out, and in the daily report this incident is recorded, and this report is sent to the ministry and to the staff. The staff in its turn in the daily reports that cover everything that it received from the secretariat provides this report to the ministry up its own line of reporting so that the ministry receives reports from two sources.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It seems to mean the same thing in the end, but perhaps the last bit added something. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, let me just follow up on this. If we encountered this situation, the investigative judge of the regular district court within whose jurisdiction this unfortunate accident occurred and the public prosecutor, they go out on the scene.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's up to the judge to decide whether they want to go to the scene or not. It sometimes happened that the investigative judge would authorise the SUP to carry out the investigation, and then the investigation would be done by the SUP itself; but it is the discretionary right of the investigative judge to decide that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me as far as the personnel of the Ministry of the Interior are concerned, who regulates how they should go about performing their work, what is the basis for the way in which those activities are regulated?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior personnel carry out their tasks on the basis of the law and other regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The Law on Internal Affairs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Law on Internal affairs, the rules on organization, the rules on interpersonal relations, and there is a number of those rules. I can't really remember all of them now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at P1737, Article 7. [In English] Article 7, please. Could we have in English also, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we can see here that the minister, or rather, could you please read Article 7 for me, please?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The minister shall determine the manner in which the Ministry of the Interior performs its duties and issue instructions for their performance."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And this is the key law as far as you're concerned?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, the Law on Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, it says here that it's the minister who determines that, but there is the rules on how the -- how this is to be carried out, just as in the military you have Rules of Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, but this is a lower act than this one, the lower instrument?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have P1992 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My colleague Mr. Lukic showed you this document yesterday, but not everything was read out. There is a sentence missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Wrong document. P1990, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a meeting at the staff held by Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic with his associates and senior officers from the republican state security sectors in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please get the lower half of the page in B/C/S and page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Colonel, sir, you read this yesterday but you didn't read the previous sentence. So can we start, please, that's the lower half of the page, roughly speaking, it's about seven lines from the bottom up, the first words are: "Has been elaborated, the plan for the public security sector has been elaborated in order to prevent access by NATO to our territory." And then on from there.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The staff planned to carry out as soon as this was ordered three actions to clear the terrain from the terrorists in the Podujevo, Dragobilje, and Drenica areas or sectors.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That will do. Let's see first who was at this meeting, was there anyone from the army who was present listed up there?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No one at all from the army?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Fine. What is RJB, is this a military organization?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the public security sector and it's part of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You were saying that these actions were executed according to an army plan, but we see no mention here of the army or indeed anyone attending from the army. Would I be right in saying that all the SUP chiefs and PJP and SAJ commanders attended this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right when you say that they will attend it, but you're not right when you suggest what you did about the plan. The plan that we discussed earlier was about taking action against the terrorists. Plans for the elimination, or rather, anti-terrorist combat, so that's not in relation to that, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, thankfully we can all read and we see what is written there. Are you trying to tell us something that is both baseless and illogical, would that be your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: If you look closely at what it says --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is not about anti-terrorist activities. This is about NATO.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you please read the same sentence again.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "A plan has been elaborated on by the RJB in order to foil and prevent NATO's access to our territory."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mijatovic. Who made this plan in the RJB?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite frank, I don't understand this sentence. I know that there were defence plans, defence plans for the eventuality of war, and this is something that's done by all the secretariats. The Ministry of the Interior at its HQ also have their own defence plan, so the reference was to all those plans together, but if this was a plan of the public security sector, then that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So all these activities make up a plan or the plan of the public security sector, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which activities you mean. I'm talking about defence plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This is all within the framework of the MUP, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And there's a legal basis for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Let's move on. Tell me about maintaining public law and order, protecting persons and property, combatting terrorism and crime, organizing the safe-guarding of vital facilities and buildings, this was also something that happened to be the job of the MUP, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Likewise, it was the MUP that devised their own system of command and their own communications system, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the MUP they don't use military terminology, they don't say "command," they say lead, not commanding, leading. In each of the ministries there's a special administration that deals with these issues, setting up a communications system specifically. In the secretariats these are termed departments or sectors, I'm not sure which.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have fifth page in English, same document, and the third page in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mijatovic, same document. It's Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic taking the floor and his words are recorded here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have the lower half of the page in the Serbian or the B/C/S. [In English] And the bottom of the page in English also, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see line 10 it says "work out a system ..." Can you please read that.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this a document? Is this a meeting? Is this the record of a meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: It's the same one that I've been showing you.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't quite find this. All right. "Work out a system of command and communications." Yes, the minister used the term -- or at least that's what he was recorded as saying, but this is not the established mode of communication within the ministry, to use the term "command." We use the term "to lead."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But that's how it reads, it reads command, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, that's true. What I was saying is that we have organizational units at the level of the ministry that deal with this kind of issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have 6D269.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: May I ask a question, please. I'd like to find out from the witness what is the distinction between commanding and leading.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I couldn't really draw a distinction there or define a distinction. I'd never spent too much time thinking about that, but the military used the term "command" and the MUP used the term - how should I put this? - it's a bit softer in a way. As I explained yesterday, all members of the police are authorised officials and they must carry out tasks under the law without waiting for special orders, as in "naradjenje," and I think that is the essence. A soldier does nothing until such time as he has received an order. I think this is the essential essence, as far as I understand, because "command" is a very tough term, it's too unwieldy for police work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, may I -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, sir, can you please look at item 1 of this document, update the defence plan. You see that, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is this the defence plan that you talked about a while ago that was done by the MUP in all the secretariats of their own?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have count 5 of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we look at this item, the Ministry of the Interior selects essential locations, organization, and ways of relocating; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please look at item 6 now, passage. It says: "Plan measures and carry out preparations for the physical security of some buildings, persons," and so on. Who planned these measures, security measures, for the safe-guarding persons, installations, and facilities of special importance?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each secretariat in relation to its own area.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have count 11 of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you please read the first sentence in item 11 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just give us a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sorry

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before we continue, it may be worth commenting that this distinction that is sought to be made between the circumstances in which a policeman might act without an order or direction and the circumstances of a soldier who acts only on orders might have some relevance to the responsibility of the police who, according to the witness, act according to the law to comply with a direction made under Articles 16 and 17 of the Law on Defence for resubordination. And we would in due course appreciate the comments of parties on that. Now, Mr. Cepic, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, sir, while we still have item 11 in front of us, can you please tell me this: Where were these command posts with reserve positions selected and prepared?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no way I can know that. Each secretariat had its own defence plan envisaging this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: It says command posts, not posts for leading, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says, but I do have to explain, don't I? This is the expression used because during a war this plan is followed, or rather, the police units are envisaged in this plan and these police units have their own commands. Therefore, this is for wartime circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Thank you. But one thing we don't have in the transcript is the term police war units. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in the plans of every secretariat, it's something that is envisaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at item 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You see item 16, right? It reads: "In the eventuality of an aggression cooperate fully" --

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: There is no talk there of resubordination or subordination. It's about cooperation, it's about exchanging information and so on and so forth, right?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's talk of the Law on Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the Law on Defence. We'll get to it later. Mr. Mijatovic, can you please listen closely to my questions and answer my questions and my questions alone?

utterances.speaker: MIROSLAV MIJATOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have P1100.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the header --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Your Honour, I don't see this document on the list from the Lazarevic Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sure it is on one of the lists, and my assistant will try to check this. I only have a single question in relation to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... then the question I think can be posed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, do you stand in your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we got the same objections all the time from the other side, so we do have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Were any of them sustained?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Or did you simply back down?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, but did they simply -- sorry, these objections to you were sustained, were they?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Without you withdrawing? All right. Well, Mr. Cepic, deal with another one just now and you can direct your attention to the notification tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Meanwhile I can ask a little question, that will give you some relief. While talking of the Ministry of Interior, you stated that the minister laid the rules or regulations which would govern the Ministry of the Interior, but then you said that this is subject to some general -- some general rules. What are those general rules? Are these the rules which govern every ministry and is laid by a parliament or is there something else? But I couldn't understand that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't, probably an expert could tell you more about that. I can talk more about -- well, what I mean is this, there is the Law on Ministries, the Law on State administration, the Law on Internal affairs and other laws, the Law on Criminal procedure and so on and so forth and the ministry bases its work on that. The minister who is part of the ministry adopts a book of rules or instructions regulating this. For example, a lawyer in the organization of the ministry, a book of rules on the work of the ministry, we saw that yesterday - I'm very tired now already - the instructions on the informing process. So he adopts these instructions based on the law. But I'm sure an expert would be better placed to talk about this and would be far more competent to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Have you found the notification?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may, my assistant has just tracked it down, and the problem is there's a 0 missing in what he wrote and we can show you a copy of that mail which he sent to all the parties involved. When we gave notice of our list, there is a 0 missing in relation to this document, it reads here P110 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have the same mistake from the Prosecutor's side and they notified us that they made a mistake, so we accept the Prosecution's point, but not this way of dealing with the things. We are ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, you're maintaining your point, are you, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you say that that's a course we followed earlier in the case where there was a mistake of this nature, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- this kind of mistake, but when we were late with the announcement of the document, the objections were sustained. But if there is a document with a number we received, then we checked that document, not the document which has one 0 less in its number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We have to finish now, so we'll tell you tomorrow. Can you tell us what we might expect from you tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps half an hour, and if I may, as far as the objection by my friend Branko Lukic is concerned, I would like to say that my memory tells me otherwise as far as my own objections were concerned and the way they were characterized. Thank you, and I hope that Judge Kamenova is feeling better today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic, we have to break again until tomorrow. Please bear in mind what I said to you about communication between these hearings. Tomorrow our continued hearing is at 2.15 in Courtroom I. Could you now please leave this court with the usher, and we will see you tomorrow again at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 14th day of February, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.32 p.m.,
